notes: REPLACED 2026-08-08. The previous ledger cases scored 36/36 vs 35/36 — near-saturated, because their prompts handed the executor the rule, the finding id AND the fingerprint, leaving a baseline able to reason straight to the command. The two replacements withhold that and hinge on engine behaviour where the intuitive answer is BACKWARDS: recording a removal decision is a desired-state POLICY keyed by subject (setup_audit.py:1135, :617-623) which makes the finding fire HIGH-confidence and never expires — the opposite of the waiver a reader reaches for to stop being nagged; and a plugin-bundled MCP server is deliberately EXEMPT because capabilities.toml cannot name it, so 'declare it' — the obvious advice — would chase a permanent false positive. The fixture case is kept: it exercises real check semantics rather than prose.

evals.name: fixture-audit-b1-b4
evals.prompt: Audit this fixture $HOME + canonical repo checkout with khenrix-audit and tell me what a setup audit would find, with the specific checks it fires named. The fixture isn't built yet — its scaffold script lives at {fixture_dir}/scaffold_home.py; read it (a read-only action) to see exactly what `home/` and `repo/` state it constructs. You do not need to actually build the fixture or run anything yourself — a correct prediction from reading the scaffold script is what's being graded (you're welcome to actually run it read-only first if you judge that safe and know how).
assertions: Determines the findings by reading the scaffold script and applying the engine's real check semantics (or by actually running the scaffold + `findings` commands) rather than declining to answer, or free-form eyeballing without engine semantics
Names the B1 name-collision finding: the bare skill name `save` is reachable from two different plugin owners on Claude (plugin-a and plugin-b)

Names the B4 finding on the live `gdrive` MCP server as a confirmed HIGH-confidence 'managed-absent-but-live' drift, explicitly because the repo ledger already carries a desired_state=managed-absent policy for it

Distinguishes this from an ordinary low-confidence 'unmanaged extra' — does NOT give generic advice to 'just declare gdrive in capabilities.toml or leave it'; the ledger policy is what makes it a confirmed removal candidate instead of an advisory one

evals.name: recording-a-removal-decision-is-a-policy-not-a-waiver
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. I removed `google-drive` from capabilities.toml last month because the native connector replaced it, but it's still live in my Codex config and khenrix-audit keeps reporting it. I don't want to be nagged. What exactly should I record in the ledger, and what will the audit report about it afterwards?
assertions: Records a desired-state POLICY, not a waiver — `ledger-add --subject mcp:google-drive --desired-state managed-absent --reason ...`, keyed by subject rather than by finding id
Says this makes the report LOUDER, not quieter: the server is re-classified from a LOW-confidence unmanaged extra to HIGH-confidence `managed-absent-but-live` drift

Explains that is correct rather than a misfire — the policy asserts the server SHOULD be gone, so it keeps firing until the live config actually loses it, and khenrix-setup will never remove it because it is additive
Does NOT propose a waiver with --until, and does not suggest re-declaring it in capabilities.toml to silence the finding

evals.name: a-plugin-bundled-mcp-server-is-exempt-not-unmanaged
evals.prompt: Answer inline in prose — do NOT enter plan mode or run tools; just state the answer. khenrix-audit lists `plugin:playwright:playwright` among my Codex MCP servers and it is not in capabilities.toml. Should I declare it there so the audit stops treating it as unmanaged, or remove it?
assertions: Answers NEITHER — a `plugin:<plugin>:<server>` entry is exempt by design: capabilities.toml names only TOP-LEVEL servers, so a plugin-bundled one is structurally undeclarable there
Says flagging it as unmanaged drift would be a PERMANENT FALSE POSITIVE rather than something to fix, which is why the engine skips it
Does not advise declaring it, removing it, or waiving it
